subtype: Approach: working backward from dates and exams [Thinking]
passage: In the students' union room the exam timetable and the hostel holiday list lay side by side on the table. Yamini ran a pencil down both. "Exams end on the ninth and the hostel shuts on the sixteenth. Only one stretch works for all of us." Farida groaned that there had to be another option, checked again, and found none. "Then train seats come first," Yamini said, "because everything else hangs on the day we leave. A room is easy to find once we know when we arrive." Farida wrote the dates on the board under the word TRAINS and left STAY blank for the following week. Two other members nodded, relieved that someone had finally chosen an order to work in.

qa.q: On which dates did Yamini say the exams end and the hostel shuts?
qa.a: The exams end on the ninth and the hostel shuts on the sixteenth.

qa.q: What was Farida feeling when Yamini said only one stretch worked?
qa.a: Farida felt frustrated and hoped for another option. After checking again Farida accepted that there was none.

qa.q: What could the group add to this plan, and why?
qa.a: They could keep a spare day at the end of the window and prefer refundable seats, since one fixed slot leaves no room if a train is cancelled.

qa.q: How might the two quieter members see Yamini's decision to fix the trains first?
qa.a: They felt relieved, because the group had been going in circles and now knew what to do next.

grounding: A group fits a trip around exam dates and holidays, books the dependent item first and settles the rest afterwards.

subtype: Approach: working backward from dates and exams [Thinking]
passage:
Hi Nilesh,
Since you're in charge of tickets, here's how I worked out our dates. Tell me if I've missed something.
My last exam is on 19 December. Yours and Meenu's end on the 20th. College reopens on 2 January, and Arif has his cousin's wedding on the 29th. So the only clean window is 21 to 28 December.
Now, everything depends on the train to Kochi. It's a 36-hour journey and the holiday trains fill up fast. If we leave on the evening of the 21st, we reach on the morning of the 23rd, and a train back on the night of the 26th gets us home on the 28th, a day before the wedding.
So please book trains first, today if you can. The homestay in Fort Kochi can wait a few days. There are plenty, and we can match them to whatever train dates we get.
Farida

qa.q: Why does Farida want the trains booked first, and how does Farida seem to feel about it?
qa.a: Farida feels a little anxious that holiday trains fill fast, and sees that every other part of the plan depends on the train dates.

qa.q: What could Nilesh do if the train on the 21st is full?
qa.a: Check the next possible train within the window and match the homestay to it, rather than booking stays first.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Arif?
qa.a: Arif can come without worry, since the dates were chosen to get everyone home before the wedding on the 29th.

grounding: Shows a student working back from exam dates and a wedding to find the one free window, then booking trains first and stays after.

subtype: Approach: working backward from dates and exams [Thinking]
passage:
Madhuri, you asked how our group of six managed Hampi in the middle of semester. This is Kiran, official calendar nerd, so here's the secret: we started from the end, not the beginning.
First I wrote down every hard date. Internal exams till 11 October. Two of us had a lab viva on the 16th. Diwali leave started on the 18th, and everyone wanted to be home for that. So the only gap was the 12th to the 15th. Four days.
Then I asked, what fixes everything else? Transport. There's one good overnight bus from our city to Hampi on those days, with only a few seats. If we didn't get it, no trip. So we booked the bus first, the same evening. Only after that did we choose a guesthouse, and there were plenty to pick from.
If we'd picked the guesthouse first, we'd have been stuck with rooms and no way to get there.

qa.q: How does Kiran feel about the plan now, looking back?
qa.a: Kiran sounds proud and pleased, calling it a secret and joking about being the calendar nerd.

qa.q: What else could the group have prepared in case the bus got cancelled?
qa.a: A backup, like a train to a nearby town, noted in advance so the four-day window still works.

qa.q: What would change for the group if they had booked the guesthouse first?
qa.a: They could have ended up with rooms and no bus seats, losing money and the only free window.

grounding: Shows a student working back from exams, a viva and Diwali leave to find a four-day window, then booking the scarce bus first and the stay after.
